summary.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the first quarter under IHC ownership, with PAT of INR243 crores after last quarter's balance-sheet markdowns. Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

financial_highlights.change: Following balance-sheet markdowns and provisions taken in the prior quarter; no YoY comparison stated
Stated as in line with guidance; no QoQ figure given
Home loans about INR664 crores; loans against property about INR2,000 crores
Described as standard in normal course of business
Down about 50 bps during the quarter
International rating upgraded from B+ to BB-

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: About INR664 crores disbursed in Q1; mortgage remains the anchor product this year.

segments.name: Loans against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About INR2,000 crores disbursed in Q1, the largest product by disbursement; micro LAP planned as a mainstay.

segments.name: Loans against securities / unsecured / credit-fund deal
segments.commentary: Loans against securities INR262 crores and unsecured about INR100 crores in Q1; one INR840 crore co-lending deal with an Asia-based credit fund (20% Sammaan, 80% fund).

guidance_outlook: Disbursements: INR10,000 crores in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crores in H2, total INR30,000 crores for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.
Cost of funds: 9.6% by September, 9.3% by end-FY27, and 7-8% range over the next 2-3 years; management said below 8% over three years.
Cost-to-income: about 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28, targeted at 30-35% by FY29.
Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27, rising to 270, with 800 branches targeted by end of FY28.
Five-year targets cited on the call: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%, as put out on May 20.
Inorganic growth to be considered from FY28; the bias for now is to build.
capex_capacity: Branch network to rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 23 master service centres across 20 states; management targets 800 branches by end of FY28.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, integrating a new Salesforce-based CRM and a new loan management system, plus a data lake.
Digital personal loans to launch on the app in H2 FY27; gold loans, two-wheeler loans and BNPL-type e-commerce tie-ups targeted by end-FY28.
53 AI use cases under implementation, with about 60% to be implemented in FY27; about 66% of identified use cases reportedly in motion.
Hiring: mid-level and ground-level offer-to-join cycle is 90-120 days; senior management hires expected to be announced towards the end of Q1/start of Q2.
demand_pricing: FY27 disbursement mix: about 75% mortgage-backed (two-thirds retail, one-third wholesale AUM with about 20% kept on balance sheet), 25% new products; about 90% secured and 10% unsecured in FY27, moving to 80:20 in FY28.

Securitisation and asset-light model: at least 30% of origination to be securitised or sold down, with 60-70% kept as a backup option; assets below 9.5% to be sold down via direct assignment, above 9.5% sliced between balance sheet and securitisation.
Asset yield universe cited from 8.5% (prime) to about 20% (unsecured); LAP 11-12% and affordable loans 12-13% also eligible for securitisation.
Fee income expected to rise, with direct assignment fee income kicking in around October 2026 with about a six-month lag.
97% of Q1 disbursements and 97% of AUM are secured.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Will lower cost of funds be passed on to customers for acquisition, or will spreads be retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rides on lower cost of funds plus asset-light model; sub-9.5% assets to be sold down via direct assignment and higher-yield assets kept or securitised, balancing fee and spread income.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): How much upfront opex and what is the cost-to-income path?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex will rise in absolute terms, offset by fee income with a lag of a quarter or two; cost-to-income around 50% this year, declining from H2 FY28, reaching 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Abhiram Iyer (Deutsche Bank): What is the asset-class breakup of the roughly INR3,000 crore per half target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 mix about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products; disbursement breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Agarwal (Bajaj Alternates): What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 90 bps saving on about INR50,000 crore borrowings (about INR450 crore annualised), targeting a further 70 bps; software procurement at 30-50% of earlier costs; and senior talent additions.

qa_highlights.question: Sanket (DAM Capital): What is IHC's larger vision beyond lending in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: Niharika (CapGrow): Are the five-year ROE, ROA and NIM targets achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident, citing rating upgrades, lower cost of funds, asset-light model and tech, with governance as the enabler.

qa_highlights.question: Nilesh Sharma (Monomer): What are disbursement targets for this and next financial year?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30,000 crores in FY27 (INR10,000 crores H1, INR20,000 crores H2) and INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.

risks_watch: Rating path: management targets AAA domestic and BB+ international in H2 FY27 to FY28, but the only upgrades so far are AA to AA+ and B+ to BB-; further upgrades drive the 9.3% year-end and 7-8% multi-year cost of funds targets.
Cost of funds delivery: incremental cost of funds is about 9% vs. the 9.6% September and 9.3% end-FY27 targets; monitor whether the quarterly pace of roughly 50 bps decline continues.

Execution ramp: disbursements must step from INR10,000 crores in H1 to INR20,000 crores in H2 FY27, with the digital-first app, digital personal loans and senior hiring all slated for H2; hiring cycle is 90-120 days.

Cost-to-income path: opex to rise in absolute terms with branches going from about 240 to 270 by end-H1 and 800 by end-FY28; cost-to-income about 50% in FY27 depends on fee income from direct assignment, expected to kick in around October 2026.

Recoveries and asset quality: management said recoveries will exceed internal projections and that no P&L pain is expected, but the Q1 PAT of INR243 crores relies on net recoveries of INR240 crores; watch recovery run-rate and ARC sale outcomes.
Five-year targets (ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%): management stated confidence but gave no interim milestones beyond FY27 targets; track progress against these.
Governance and inorganic plans: statutory auditor change and internal audit co-sourcing partner selection were said to be closing this quarter; inorganic growth deferred to FY28.
key_quotes: The incremental cost of fund is now down to about 9%.
First quarter was bang on target, and that will increase to INR20,000 crores in the second half.
So we're obviously confident which is why we mustered the courage to put it on in public domain and hold ourselves accountable to that.
This year is a year of stabilization of NBFC, of putting the building blocks together.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on the cost of funds, disbursement and recovery trajectory, and on the IHC benefits, with repeated 'bang on target' and '100% confidence' language. It was more hedged on the five-year targets' feasibility, senior-hire timing and the Dalia Khorshid response on non-lending India plans, which management said is a year away from decisions.

adds.what: Branch network from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 800 branches targeted by end of FY28
Digital-first app with Salesforce-based CRM and new loan management system (go-live)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 disbursements of INR30,000 crores (H1 INR10,000 cr, H2 INR20,000 cr) and FY28 INR40,000-50,000 crores, backed by branch expansion from ~240 to 270 and 800 by FY28 and new digital/LAP products, but with no concrete order or capacity numbers beyond branch counts and mostly plans rather than commissioned capacity.

mgmt.note: Senior management hires expected to be announced towards end of Q1/start of Q2; management reiterated shift from portfolio management to growth.
